## The response and the panel

Each row records satellite-detected burned area divided by county land area for one month.
The MODIS MCD64A1 burned-area product detects managed burning as well as wildfire.
The modelling domain is a fixed set of 3,108 counties over January 2003–December 2024:
820,512 county-month rows.

An observed zero and a missing observation are different. An absent annual export, a
missing county-month key, or an invalid numerical target must fail preparation rather than
become zero fire. The local input audit checks the 22 annual shards, the full unique key set,
and agreement between the raw burned-area ratios and all three model splits.

The response measures satellite detections. A recorded zero does not by itself
establish complete satellite coverage or the absence of physical burning. The
analysis does not impose a minimum mapped-area coverage threshold.

In particular, `Uncertainty` describes burn-date uncertainty. Valid input coverage is
encoded in QA bit 1, while bit 2 flags a shortened mapping period.
[Official MCD64A1 documentation](https://developers.google.com/earth-engine/datasets/catalog/MODIS_061_MCD64A1).

## The feature set for this release

The models use fixed geography, known calendar features, and observed response history.

| Retained input | Construction |
|---|---|
| Elevation and slope | Fixed county terrain values |
| Aspect sine and cosine | Fixed terrain orientation, avoiding the 0°/360° discontinuity |
| Calendar harmonics | Known target month encoded by sine/cosine pairs |
| Burned-area and occurrence history | Observations at or before the forecast origin |
| County graph and identity | Fixed geography; neighbor histories or learned representations |
| XGBoost county summaries | Expanding response means/rates using months strictly before origin |

Terrain is frozen from the first training month and then reused. Its training-only
normalization is checked against the raw panel. Later copies of terrain cannot change
an earlier feature vector. The retained terrain values need no missing-value imputation.

The models do not use population, built area, land-cover fractions or categories,
fuel cover, target-month weather, drought, vegetation, or snow. For example, interpolating
a 2016 population value between 2015 and 2020 would import a later source into an earlier
row. Dropping the entire column removes that dependency.

This compact information set supports forecasting from geography, season, and fire history.

## Chronological windows

The panel has three contiguous target periods:

| Split | Months | Panel rows |
|---|---|---:|
| Train | January 2003–May 2018 | 574,980 |
| Test | June 2018–July 2020 | 80,808 |
| Validation | August 2020–December 2024 | 164,724 |

For origin $o$, both models use a 48-month history ending at $o$ and predict the next
twelve months. Assign a window only when all twelve target months belong to the same split.

```python
history = slice(origin - lookback + 1, origin + 1)
targets = slice(origin + 1, origin + horizon + 1)

assert origin - lookback + 1 >= 0
assert origin + horizon < number_of_months
assert all(target_split[t] == selected_split
           for t in range(origin + 1, origin + horizon + 1))
```

A lag must satisfy both bounds, $0\le\text{history index}\le o$. Python's negative
indices wrap to the end of an array, so an upper-bound check alone is insufficient.

A later origin may use earlier observed responses from another split as history.
For example, a validation-origin forecast can use already observed test-period burns.
That is the intended rolling prediction policy, not permission to use outcomes after
that forecast's origin. The entire validation period is not one forecast issued at
its beginning.

The evaluation assumes burned-area observations through the stated origin are available.

## Training-derived summaries and preprocessing

A county mean computed over the entire training period would expose early training rows
to their own responses and to later training outcomes. XGBoost's expanding summary at
origin $o$ is

$$
\bar y_{c,o}=\frac{1}{o}\sum_{t=0}^{o-1}y_{ct},
$$

with the occurrence rate constructed the same way. It is computed before the origin.
Other explicit lags may use the observed response at $o$, but none uses a target at $o+h$.
There is no climatology target-encoding feature in this experiment.

The expanding summary uses all earlier recorded months, not only the 48-month sequence
window. That is a different representation of past information from the GNN's finite
encoder and learned county embedding; it does not introduce a future response.

The shared preprocessing code permits only forward filling from earlier predictor
observations and rejects unresolved leading gaps. It never backfills from test into
train, or from validation into an earlier period. Missing targets cannot be imputed.

Scalers are fitted on training data and applied unchanged to later splits.
Annual land-cover categories cannot enter through a global vocabulary:
the GNN omits that embedding, and the booster's remaining schema placeholder is constant.

## What the leakage checks exercise

Small adversarial tests alter future responses and excluded covariates, then verify that
earlier feature vectors and predictions remain unchanged. Positive controls alter legal
history and verify that the relevant inputs do change. Separate tests check window bounds,
complete split-contained horizons, and the strictly past county summaries.

The source audit also verifies that the stored targets match the raw exports, that retained
terrain is constant apart from numerical reduction roundoff, and that its saved scaling
uses only training moments. The fitted models, data files, code, and generated report
are tied together by hashes.

These checks address feature separation. They do not establish satellite observation
completeness, performance in unseen counties, or real-time availability of every input.
